div.p: What HE said to his heart when leaving after the union.

lg.l: yāma viravi ṉeṭuṅkaṭai niṉṟu
tēmutir cimaiya kuṉṟam pāṭu
nuṇkō lakavu[na]r vēṇṭiṉ veṇkōṭ
ṭaṇṇal yāṉai yīyum vaṇmakiḻ
veḷiyaṉ veṇmā ṉāa yeyiṉa
ṉaḷiyiyal vāḻkkaip pāḻip paṟantalai
yiḻaiyaṇi yāṉai yiyaṟēr miñiliyoṭu
naṇpaka luṟṟa ceruviṟ puṇkūrn
toḷvāṇ mayaṅkamar [vī]ḻnteṉap puḷḷoruṅ
kaṅkaṇ vicumpiṉ viḷaṅku ñāyiṟ
ṟoṇkatir te[ṟā]maṟ ciṟakariṟ kōli
niḻalcey tuḻaṟal kāṇeṉac ciṉai[i]p
paṭukaḷaṅ kāṇṭal cellāṉ ciṉañciṟan
turuviṉai na[ṉṉa] ṉaruḷaṉ cāyap
peruvitup puṟṟa palvēṇ makaḷir
kurū[u]ppūm paintā rarukkiya pūcal
varaiviṭak kaṭakkum vayaṅkuperun tāṉai
yakutai taḷa[rvu]tī[r]n tāṅku mikupeya
luppucciṟai nillā veḷḷam pōla
nāṇuvarai nillāk kāma naṇṇi
nalkiṉaḷ vāḻiyar vantē yōri
palpaḻap palaviṉ payaṅkeḻu kollik
kārmalar kaṭuppa nāṟu
mērnuṇ ṇōti māa yōḷē.
Like a flood that does not stop before a salt ridge
in the ample rain, as if the slackening of Akutai had ended,
with a shining big army that excels, beyond the limit,
in a clamour, which makes brilliant flowers [meant] for fresh garlands scarce,
of many ladies of the Vēḷ [clan] who felt great haste,
when merciless Naṉṉaṉ of fearful work died,
exceeding in [his] anger, he who could not see the battle field,
as a disturbance arose – look – throwing a shadow,
as birds’ wings together interlaced without being scorched
by the bright beams of the sun shining in the fine-spaced(?) sky,
as they descended on the confuse battle of bright swords,
wounds abounding in the fight that took place at high noon,
with Miñili on a chariot moving forward with a jewel-adorned elephant,
by the desert village of Pāḻi, with a living of caring nature,
Āay, the hunter, with white horses, Veḷiyaṉ,
with liberal toddy, who gives superior elephants
with white tusks, when singers with fine staffs want [them],
who sing of the hill with honey-ripening peaks,
standing [there] at the long edge of midnight
coming, she drew near [and] granted – may she live –
passion that does not stop before the boundary of shame,
the dark one with pretty fine hair,
fragrant so as to resemble blossoms in monsoon time
from Kolli [hill] rich in the yield of jackfruit trees with many fruits.
